chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn al-Jallab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) did not make al-ghayrah (sense of honor/jealousy) for the women, and rather it is the evil ones of them who express it; as for the believing women, they do not. But rather, Allah made al-ghayrah for the men because He permitted the man four (wives) and whatever his right hand possesses, and did not make it for the woman except for her husband. So if she were to intend someone else along with him, she would be an adulteress in the Presence of Allah.

He said, and Al-Qasim ibn Yahya reported it from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), except that he said: 'So if she were to be immoral with someone else along with him'.

key_terms.الْغَيْرَةُ: Sense of honor, jealousy, or protective zeal
key_terms.مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُهُ: What his right hand possesses (concubines/slave girls)

ai.seo_question: Why is the sense of honor (al-ghayrah) designated for men rather than women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith distinguishes between 'ghayrah' (protective jealousy/honor) and 'ghirah' (possessive jealousy), asserting that the former is a masculine trait aligned with the asymmetry of marital rights (polygyny for men, monogamy for women). The variant reading 'baghat' (committed fornication) in the chain of Qasim ibn Yahya emphasizes the legal consequence of a woman seeking extra-marital relations, reinforcing the theological link between gender-specific rights and spiritual accountability.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Sa’ad Bin Al Jallab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Make the sense of ‘الْغَيْرَةُ’ (honour of lineage) to be for the women, and rather it is the evil ones of them who express it, and as for the Believing women, so they don’t. But rather, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made the sense of ‘الْغَيْرَةُ’ to be for the men because He<sup>azwj</sup> Permitted four (wives) for the men and whatever his right hands possess (slave girls), and did not Make it to be for the women except for her (one) husband. So if she were to intend someone else along with him, she would be an adulteress in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And it has been reported by Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So if she were to be immoral with someone else along with him’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Sa‘d al-Jallab who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has not placed pride in women. Such feeling comes from detested ones among them; however, the believing ones of them are free of pride. Allah has placed pride in men; He has made lawful for men up to four and those whom they own (slaves). For women He has made only their husband so if she wants more besides him she is a fornicator before Allah.’

He (the narrator) has said that al-Qasim ibn Yahya has narrated from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Bakr al-Hadramiy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, except that he has said, ‘Baghat’ (sought) instead of ‘Aradat’ (wanted).”
